niche_preference_profile: This user prefers UIs that feel complete, clearly structured, and easy to scan, with enough visible content to feel useful but not so much that the screen feels cluttered. They like strong hierarchy, explicit labels, visible actions, and clear sectioning. They generally prefer lighter, cleaner, more conventional settings-style layouts over dark/heavy or overly decorative ones, but they also want the interface to avoid dead space and feel populated and finished. In alerts and modals, they prefer calm, focused, isolated dialogs with concise copy and restrained action styling.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that show a full, populated set of items or settings rather than sparse, empty, or placeholder-like content.
Prefers strong visual hierarchy with clear titles, section labels, grouped content, and obvious separation between parts of the screen.
Prefers prominent, easy-to-find primary actions such as Add, Next, or a clear CTA button.
Prefers list rows or cards that expose per-item actions directly, such as unblock, delete, info, or editable controls.
Prefers items to show enough identity cues to be recognizable, such as names, phone numbers, avatars, initials, or other labels.
Prefers familiar settings-screen patterns with standard rows, toggles, chevrons, and organized categories over custom or unusual arrangements.
Prefers layouts that use the available space well and avoid large unused blank areas, while still staying readable.
Prefers direct, concise, functional copy over verbose, marketing-like, or overly explanatory text.
Prefers screens that are easy to scan quickly, with fewer competing elements and less visual clutter.
Prefers search fields that clearly state what can be searched, and that feel integrated and usable rather than vague or isolated.
Often prefers light, airy, cleaner visual styling with softer surfaces and less heavy framing.
Prefers readable text and controls with strong contrast and clear legibility.
In modal or alert states, prefers calm, isolated dialogs with concise messaging and less aggressive visual treatment.
Prefers progress indicators that are understandable and visible without adding clutter, especially in setup flows.
